headline: Priced for a collapse in local assembly: at PKR 1,394.80 the market implies shrinking sales; our base case values SAZEW at about PKR 2,289, but the Auto Policy 2026-31 outcome is close to binary
executive_summary: Sazgar has become a scaled four-wheeler assembler for GWM (Haval, Tank, ORA) and BAIC on top of its three-wheeler franchise: FY26 revenue was PKR 191,715m (+76.4%) and net profit PKR 23,605m, EPS 390.51 [EV-0002, EV-0027].

The share trades at 3.6x trailing earnings with net cash of about PKR 10.2bn at 30 September 2026 [EV-0001, EV-0003]. Reverse DCF: holding our margins, the price requires revenue to shrink about 2.0% a year for seven years, or EBIT margins of about 9.0% against 13.7% in our base case.

Our base case (revenue +12% in FY27E, EBIT margin fading from 15.0% to 12.5%, 21.5% cost of equity in PKR) gives a DCF value of PKR 2,268 and a reliability-weighted fair value of PKR 2,289; the bear and bull cases span PKR 1,102 to PKR 3,318 (interpretation: the margin of safety exists even in the bear case, but not in the policy-stress case of PKR 559).

The near-term trend is weakening, not improving: Q1 FY27 four-wheeler units fell 11.81% while three-wheelers rose 44.69%, and the company absorbed the sales-tax rise on hybrids, cutting operating profit to PKR 6,148m from PKR 6,809m [EV-0010, EV-0003].

The decisive variable is policy: customs duties on imported CBU vehicles were reduced from July 2026 and the Auto Policy 2026-31 was still pending at quarter end; management itself warns of declining local production without an adequate tariff differential [EV-0010].

thesis_pillars.title: The price discounts a structural collapse that the evidence does not (yet) show
thesis_pillars.argument: At 3.6x trailing earnings the market requires about -2.0% annual revenue decline or a 9.0% EBIT margin to justify the price. Q1 FY27 revenue still grew to PKR 41,711m from PKR 33,825m and the order book shifted towards higher-value models (favourable mix) [EV-0010]. Our base case already haircuts margins from 19.0% (FY26) to 12.5% (interpretation).

thesis_pillars.title: Capacity, product pipeline and balance sheet give room to absorb a downturn
thesis_pillars.argument: The PKR 11.50bn four-wheeler expansion is complete (capacity 54,000 units a year on a single shift) and a further PKR 22.00bn plan (fully automatic paint shop) was approved; new CKD PHEV/HEV models (Haval H6 PHEV, Tank 500 PHEV and HEV) were launched [EV-0004, EV-0027]. Cash of PKR 18,041m against debt of about PKR 7.8bn at 30 September 2026 and an A+ credit rating (VIS) reduce financing risk [EV-0003, EV-0027].

thesis_pillars.title: Three-wheelers are a cash-generative hedge against the car cycle
thesis_pillars.argument: Three-wheeler units rose 44.69% in Q1 FY27 and revenue from the segment rose to PKR 3,135.79m from PKR 2,017.87m; management expects the segment to remain an important contributor, with exports being pursued (Japan among markets) [EV-0010, EV-0004]. It is small (about 8% of Q1 sales) so it cushions rather than offsets a four-wheeler downturn (interpretation).

priced_in: The reverse DCF on the same model shows the PKR 1,394.80 price is consistent with revenue falling about 2.0% a year over seven years at our margins, or with an average EBIT margin of about 9.0% at our growth (base case 13.7%). Peers on the PSX trade at a median 6.1x trailing P/E versus about 3.6x for SAZEW [EV-0021, EV-0022, EV-0024, EV-0025, EV-0001]. The market is therefore pricing a sharp loss of competitiveness for locally assembled vehicles (interpretation), consistent with the CBU duty cuts and the pending Auto Policy flagged by management [EV-0010].
variant_perception: We agree the FY25-FY26 margins (23.6% and 19.0% EBIT) were cyclical peaks and build in further compression to 12.5%. Where we differ is on volume: the evidence shows a mix-driven revenue increase in Q1 FY27, completed capacity, new PHEV/HEV CKD models and a growing three-wheeler business [EV-0010, EV-0027, EV-0004], whereas the price implies outright shrinkage. Our view is an interpretation of policy outcomes that are not yet known; if the Auto Policy materially narrows the tariff differential the market will be right (see stress case).
business_analysis: Sazgar assembles and markets four-wheelers under Chinese brands BAIC and GWM (Haval, Tank, ORA) through 20+ four-wheeler dealers, three-wheelers (auto-rickshaws, petrol and EV variants) under the SAZGAR brand through 50+ booking agents, and automotive parts (tractor wheel rims mainly for Millat Tractors and Al-Ghazi Tractors) [EV-0027, EV-0004]. No customer exceeds 10% of sales and exports were only PKR 78.34m in FY26 [EV-0027]. The home-appliances business was discontinued from 1 September 2025 [EV-0004]. Revenue is almost entirely domestic and four-wheelers were PKR 38,443.07m of PKR 41,711m Q1 FY27 sales, so the company is effectively a single-country, single-segment cyclical [EV-0010]. Customer advances are a key funding source: trade and other payables were PKR 28,193m at 30 September 2026, against stock-in-trade of PKR 41,771m [EV-0003] - a sudden slowdown in bookings would reverse this funding (interpretation).
industry_analysis: Industry volumes are recovering: auto sector sales rose 27.71% in Q1 FY27 and four-wheelers (excluding tractors) 20.57% (source cited by the company: RAMA) [EV-0010]. Sazgar's four-wheeler units nevertheless fell 11.81%, implying share loss in the quarter (interpretation), which management links to delayed Auto Policy finalisation hitting NEV bookings [EV-0010]. Competition is intensifying with new manufacturers, expansion of existing assemblers and the shift to NEVs [EV-0005]. Key input exposures are CKD kit availability and prices, and PKR depreciation; the annual report quantifies the sensitivity of pre-tax profit to a 1% PKR move on foreign-currency balances (financial risk note) [EV-0007, EV-0002].
financial_assessment: Growth has been exceptional but cash conversion poor. Revenue grew from PKR 4,034m (FY21) to PKR 191,715m (FY26) and EBIT margin from 2.7% to 19.0% [EV-0002]. However operating cash flow fell to PKR 9,598m in FY26 from PKR 14,115m as inventory rose to PKR 42,068m and tax payments increased; the 3-year average FCF/net income is only 0.19x and the accruals ratio is 22.7% (computed flags). Capex of PKR 15,637m in FY26 funded the expansion, partly with new diminishing musharakah financing (PKR 5.2bn) [EV-0002, EV-0004]. The balance sheet reconciles in every year (FY21-FY26) and the platform resolved one OCR conflict in the audited profit and loss account (finance cost) using accounting identities (see discrepancy log). Tax is a heavy 39% (29% corporate plus 10% super tax) [EV-0002].
forecast_rationale: Revenue +12% in FY27E (Q1 +23% on mix but four-wheeler units -11.81%), +15% in FY28E as new capacity and models ramp, fading to 7% nominal PKR by FY33E; EBIT margin from 15.0% to 12.5% to reflect competition and tariff erosion; capex at about 5% of revenue for FY27E-FY28E for the PKR 22.00bn plan, then about 2%; depreciation rising from 0.45% to 1.7% of revenue as the expansions are capitalised; tax 39%. All are labelled analyst assumptions with evidence ids in the workbook [EV-0010, EV-0004, EV-0005].
governance_capital_allocation: Free float is 35% (21,156,087 shares) [EV-0001], so control rests with the sponsors; the CEO (Mian Asad Hameed), the chairperson (Mrs. Saira Asad Hameed) and the COO of the car division (Mian Muhammad Ali Hameed) share the family name [EV-0027] - a related-party and succession question we could not test further (evidence gap: pattern of shareholding and related-party note not analysed). Dividends rose to PKR 70 per share for FY26 (payout about 18%) and an interim PKR 5 was declared for Q1 FY27 [EV-0002, EV-0010]. Capital allocation is mostly reinvestment in capacity, but the purchase of two commercial plots in Lahore (Pine Avenue and CBD) is non-core and warrants scrutiny [EV-0027].

counter_thesis.argument: SAZEW's earnings are a policy artefact: CKD assemblers enjoyed a protected market, and with CBU duties cut from July 2026 and an Auto Policy that may further reduce protection, imported vehicles and new Chinese entrants could compress local volumes and margins far below our base case. Q1 FY27 already shows four-wheeler units -11.81%, margin pressure from absorbed taxes, weak cash conversion (FCF/net income 0.19x) and an inventory of PKR 41,771m that could need discounting. On this view peak-cycle earnings deserve a 3-4x multiple and the stock is fairly priced or expensive.
counter_thesis.evaluation: The counter-thesis is credible and is the main reason confidence is only MEDIUM. Evidence supports parts of it (unit decline, tax absorption, inventory build, management's own warning about local production) [EV-0010, EV-0003]. Against it: revenue still grew in Q1, the company has net cash, an A+ rating and new PHEV/HEV CKD models [EV-0027], and our base case already assumes margins well below FY26. Our stress case (growth -25pp for two years, margin -8pp) gives PKR 559, which quantifies the downside if the counter-thesis proves right.

catalysts.event: Announcement of the Auto Policy 2026-31 (tariff differential for CKD vs CBU, NEV incentives)
catalysts.timing: Pending at 30 September 2026; date not announced
catalysts.dependency: Government decision; outcome determines whether the bear/stress or base/bull case applies

catalysts.event: Monthly production and sales disclosures (four- and three-wheelers) on PSX
catalysts.dependency: Booking conversion after the policy decision

catalysts.event: Commissioning of the fully automatic paint shop under the PKR 22.00bn expansion plan

catalysts.timing: Estimated late January to February 2027 (not dated by evidence)
catalysts.dependency: Whether margin pressure from absorbed sales tax persists

risks.risk: Loss of tariff protection (CBU duty cuts, Auto Policy 2026-31)
risks.transmission: cheaper imported vehicles -> lower local CKD volumes and pricing -> revenue growth and EBIT margin -> FCFF and terminal value (stress case PKR 559)
risks.monitoring: Auto Policy notification; customs duty schedule; monthly unit sales

risks.risk: Taxes absorbed rather than passed on
risks.transmission: higher sales tax on hybrids (8.50%/12.75% to 18%) absorbed -> lower net price -> gross margin
slower bookings -> lower customer advances and higher inventory -> negative operating cash flow -> funding needs during the PKR 22.00bn capex plan
risks.monitoring: Trade and other payables vs stock-in-trade each quarter

risks.transmission: weaker PKR or LC restrictions -> higher kit cost or production stoppage -> gross margin and volumes
risks.monitoring: PKR/USD; SBP import regulations; plant shutdown notices

risks.transmission: new entrants and price competition -> market share and discounts -> volume and margin
non-core land purchases or related-party transactions -> cash diverted from operations -> lower FCFE to minorities
risks.monitoring: Related-party note; capex breakdown; pattern of shareholding

impact_matrix.transmission: tariff differential -> local volumes and price -> revenue and EBIT margin -> value
absorbed tax -> net price -> gross margin
share loss -> volumes -> revenue and operating leverage
PKR depreciation -> CKD cost -> gross margin

impact_matrix.probability: policy rate held at 11.50% in Q1 FY27
impact_matrix.transmission: rates -> financed demand and discount rate -> volumes and WACC
capex -> FCFF in FY27-FY28 and capacity for growth
country risk premium 9.71% -> cost of equity 21.5% -> value

upside_requirements: Upside to our PKR 2,268-3,318 range requires an Auto Policy that preserves a meaningful CKD/CBU tariff differential, recovery in four-wheeler units with the new PHEV/HEV models, margins holding near 15% rather than falling to the 9% the price implies, and a normalisation of working capital as the expansion completes [EV-0010, EV-0027].
downside_triggers: A policy that sharply narrows tariff protection, continued four-wheeler unit declines while the industry grows, further absorbed taxes, or an inventory write-down. Our bear case (growth -8pp, margin -4pp, WACC +0.5pp) gives PKR 1,102 and the stress case PKR 559.
falsification: Auto Policy 2026-31 cuts the CKD/CBU tariff differential materially and monthly four-wheeler units fall more than 25% year on year for two consecutive quarters.
EBIT margin below 10% for two consecutive quarters without a one-off explanation.
Operating cash flow negative for FY27 while capex stays above PKR 10bn, forcing new borrowing or a dividend cut.
dominant_assumptions: EBIT margin path (base 15.0% to 12.5%): each 1pp shift in every year moves value by about 8% (engine margin x growth grid: PKR 2,084 to PKR 2,452 for -1pp/+1pp).
Revenue growth path, which depends on the Auto Policy outcome: each 1pp in every year moves value by about 4% (PKR 2,177 to PKR 2,364).
Cost of equity of 21.5% (including the 9.71% Pakistan country risk premium) and the 5.0% nominal PKR terminal growth assumption; terminal value is 42% of EV.
evidence_gaps: No dated Auto Policy 2026-31 text or tariff schedule was retrieved; the policy outcome is unknown.
No monthly industry (PAMA) or company unit series was analysed beyond the Q1 FY27 report; the retrieved monthly production/sales disclosures were image PDFs without extractable text.
Pattern of shareholding, related-party transactions and remuneration were not analysed.
No sourced broker consensus for PSX autos was accessible; none is used.
Price history from PSX is not available to non-browser clients, so beta is bottom-up (Damodaran EM Auto & Truck) rather than a regression.
Country risk data (Damodaran) is dated 5 January 2026.
confidence_rationale: Historical financials are audited, cross-checked between documents and reconcile; cost-of-capital inputs are sourced and dated. Confidence is limited by a near-binary policy decision, a weakening Q1 trend in four-wheelers, poor cash conversion and the evidence gaps listed.
